title: Microsoft Purview Endpoint DLP: hyperlinks in Edge warn and block notifications (GCC, GCC High, DoD)
summary: Hold: the sources describe adding notification hyperlinks, but do not establish that existing Edge notifications remain unchanged without administrator action. The notification control's Learn link documents enforcement actions rather than notification customisation, and the claim that staff time is the only added cost goes beyond the published licensing evidence.

claims.where: What's changing; Open questions: Edge rendering
claims.claim: Learn does not specifically describe how the hyperlink renders in Edge notifications.
claims.quote: Searched: Endpoint DLP Edge custom notification hyperlink default configure notification title Get Support tenant wide PowerShell. Read dlp-policy-reference, microsoft-edge-security-dlp and dlp-use-notifications-and-policy-tips; no Edge-specific hyperlink rendering is described.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; summary; Why it matters; rationales: risk and impact
claims.claim: The change is admin-opt-in and existing notifications stay unchanged unless an administrator adds a hyperlink.
claims.quote: Searched: Endpoint DLP custom notification default hyperlink; Endpoint DLP Edge hyperlinks notification static text no new data default unchanged. Read the roadmap, dlp-policy-reference and Edge DLP pages; they do not state arrival behaviour or handling of existing links.
claims.fix: Set defaultState to 'unknown'. Replace the summary's second sentence and the 'Nothing appears unless' sentence with 'Microsoft has not stated what happens to existing notifications on arrival.' Remove 'only where an administrator has added one' from the impact rationale; describe adding links as an option, not a confirmed rollout default.

claims.claim: The hyperlink is static text in the rule.
claims.quote: Searched: Endpoint DLP Edge hyperlinks notification static text no new data default unchanged. Read dlp-policy-reference: it requires a resolvable URL but does not state that the hyperlink is static text.
claims.fix: Replace 'the hyperlink is static text in the rule' with 'the hyperlink must be a resolvable URL', citing https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/dlp-policy-reference.

claims.claim: The feature reads no new data.
claims.quote: Searched: Endpoint DLP Edge hyperlinks notification static text no new data default unchanged. Opened dlp-policy-reference and microsoft-edge-security-dlp; neither describes the new hyperlink feature's data reads.
claims.fix: Remove 'No change' and 'the feature reads no new data' from the Data exposure bullet.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Adding a hyperlink does not change auditing, warning or blocking behaviour.
claims.quote: Searched: Endpoint DLP Edge hyperlinks notification static text no new data default unchanged. Read dlp-policy-reference and the block-and-override scenario; they document actions and notification options separately but do not state that this feature leaves enforcement unchanged.
claims.fix: Remove 'No change: the link does not alter whether an action is audited, warned or blocked' and 'not what the rule allows or blocks' from the risk rationale. Retain the documented statement that rule actions configure enforcement.

claims.claim: Rule actions configure auditing, blocking and block-with-override for browser activities.
claims.quote: Scroll down to the Actions > Audit or restrict activities on Windows device section and set both options under the Service domain and browser activities to Block with override.

claims.claim: Custom policy tips can come from the most restrictive rule rather than the rule performing the restriction.
claims.quote: Custom Policy Tips show for the most restrictive rule, not necessarily the rule that's performing the restriction.

claims.claim: Endpoint DLP requires onboarded devices and a DLP policy including the Devices location.
claims.quote: Microsoft Endpoint DLP allows you to monitor onboarded Windows 10, and Windows 11 and onboarded macOS devices running any of the three latest released versions. Once a device is onboarded, DLP detects when sensitive items are used and shared.
claims.fix: Add https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/endpoint-dlp-getting-started to sources for onboarding. The cited enforcement scenario already identifies Devices as its monitoring location.

claims.claim: The printed Purview path reaches Service domain and browser activities in an existing rule.
claims.quote: Sign in to the Microsoft Purview portal > Data loss prevention > Policies. Choose Edit policy. Go to the Customize advanced DLP rules page ... Actions > Audit or restrict activities on Windows device ... Service domain and browser activities ... Block with override.
claims.fix: For the demonstrated warn setting, complete the path as 'Data loss prevention > Policies > policy > Edit policy > Customize advanced DLP rules > rule > Actions > Audit or restrict activities on Windows device > Service domain and browser activities > Block with override'.

claims.claim: Set-DlpComplianceRule -Identity <rule> -EndpointDlpRestrictions with a Setting/Value hashtable and Value Warn sets a rule's Endpoint DLP restrictions.
claims.quote: The EndpointDlpRestrictions parameter specifies the restricted endpoints for Endpoint DLP. The available values for <Value> are: Audit, Block, Ignore, or Warn. The Identity parameter specifies the DLP rule that you want to modify.
